column1: # gemdos-mc-fs24.tsv -- DUMPBIOS, Dsetpath after a media change: does the
# call meet it or not (TASK/FS24), against EmuTOS 1a7484ab
# gemdos-mc-paths.tsv case 67 (S04): after Dsetpath(C:\SUB) with a change
# pending, EmuTOS' Mediach(2) is still 2 -- xchdir is findit
# (bdos/fsdir.c:1113-1151), which finds a folder logged in C:'s DND tree
# without a disk access (bdos/fsdir.c:1458-1483) and touches the disk only
# through dirscan, when the parent has no logged child or the name is not
# among them; a disk access meets the change (getbcb's Mediach on a buffer
# hit, bdos/fsbuf.c:177-191; the logical Rwabs of a miss returns E_CHNG,
# bios/blkdev.c:450-451), osif logs C: in again (freetree, mark_bcbs_invalid)
# and restarts the call (bdos/bdosmain.c:449-487).  scan logs every folder
# it reads up to and including the entry it stops at (bdos/fsdir.c:1557-1574).
#   part L, S  case 67's setup, lines as gemdos-mc-paths.tsv L01-L17 and
#              S01-S07: the root and C:\SUB listed, then Dsetpath(C:\SUB)
#   part V1    a name that is not logged: V1a right after a re-login (no
#              child logged, no buffer of C:), V1b a name that does not exist
#   part V2    the root's first entry is a file (NEWDESK.INF; the order of the
#              test image's root, measured by gemdos-mc-paths L03-L08): an
#              Fsfirst for it reads the root's first sector but logs no
#   part V3    the root listed (C:\SUB logged), then a file written in C:\SUB
#              in pieces -- traffic through the sector buffers between the
#              listing and the change -- then Dsetpath(C:\SUB)
# Each part starts after a re-login (a Dfree that meets an armed change), so
# C:'s DND tree holds only its root and no buffer of C: is valid; a part
# that may leave the change pending ends with a Dfree, which meets it,
# before the next part's read prelude (a logical Rwabs returns E_CHNG while
# The DTA is buffer 1 (Fsetdta), read through the layout of
# docs/api/structures/dta.md (d:dta); only Fsetdta and Fsfirst poison it.
# A path string's bytes are compared as bytes (Dgetpath, 0:16).
# WHERE IT RUNS, DESTRUCTIVE, the test image of the gemdos-mc tables
# leaves C:\SUB\FILL.DAT (100 + 9 x 1024 bytes of buffer 0) behind; every
# change is armed by writing C:'s sector 0 back unchanged.
# One table per round: a case id is the physical line number and the dump
# header carries the CRC of this file, so it is frozen once measured.
# ---- part L: case 67's setup, the root and C:\SUB listed (gemdos-mc-paths L01-L17)
